audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: Karma wins 46.67% over 75 games but the content chart hands her 6 of 7 stages. The full layer disagreed with the content layer on five of seven rows as well (rows 0,1,2,3,5).
audit.why: Karma's real edge is levels 1-5: Lunar Rush is 22s at rank 1, Crescent Strike reaches 900 against her 950 Q, and Diana cannot dash for free without a Moonlight mark. From level 6 Moonfall drags Karma in from 475 on a 100s cooldown, and after Diana's first item that same marked-dash sequence kills rather than chunks. Karma has no dash and one 10s shield, so she does not reclaim the late game.
audit.corrected: Both layers now read Karma/Karma/Karma/Karma/Diana/Diana/Diana, with every why rewritten to match, and the late-game prose that claimed Karma out-scales Diana replaced.
sources: brief.packet winRate 46.67 / 75 games and the levelChart defect
brief.enemyKit Diana E cd 22/20/18/16/14, R cd 100/90/80 range 475

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why said 'No new ult — your 6 is a Mantra rank... press the early lead before scaling lanes wake up' on a row already marked Diana, and spikes[2].text hedged with 'still generally keep you safe'.
audit.why: Diana's level 6 is Moonfall, 100/90/80s, 475 range, pulling and slowing. Karma's is a Mantra rank. That is the spike that ends her window, and the first-item spike compounds it.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, phases[5].why and spikes[2].text now state the real spikes with numbers and no hedge.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and said only 'Moonlight marks reset her dash'.
audit.why: The precise mechanic is stronger than 'reset': Lunar Rush has NO cooldown when used onto a target afflicted with Moonlight, and Crescent Strike is 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s. Dodge the arc and her dash stays on its 22/20/18/16/14s. Pale Cascade is 15/13.5/12/10.5/9s and its shield strengthens if the third sphere detonates, so poking into the shield window wastes the poke.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, tradeGood, tradeBad, report[5].t and the dos/donts now carry those numbers and the free-dash condition.
sources: brief.enemyKit Diana Q/W/E cds and E text 'no cooldown when used to dash to an enemy afflicted with Moonlight'

audit.whatIsWrong: Eleven fields addressed Diana as he/his, and dosFull[1].d / dontsFull[2].d were the tradeGood / tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.why: Diana is female per champ-gender.js, and a Do's bullet titled 'RE + W the dive package' explaining a poke trade tells the reader nothing about the dive.
audit.corrected: All misgendered fields corrected; both bled bullets rewritten to match their own titles.

edits.before: Level 6 is the one moment you need to respect her — Moonfall can pull you in for a follow-up all-in or set up a jungler gank, so ward river and don't get caught out of position right as she hits it. Beyond that single spike window though, your poke and shields still outpace her burst even once she has her first item, since she has to close distance through your damage to land a kill. Keep playing at range, punish cooldowns, and don't let a single missed ward turn into a lost tempo swing. The lane stays in your favor through this stretch as long as you respect the level 6 all-in threat.
edits.after: Level 6 is where this turns — Moonfall pulls you in from 475 range on a 100s cooldown, and with Crescent Strike marking you her Lunar Rush costs nothing to follow up, so ward river and never stand marked. Once she completes her first item that same sequence kills you outright instead of chunking you, and you own no dash to break it, only a 10s Soul Shield. Play at max range, punish the 22s window whenever she whiffs the arc, and take plates instead of duels. From here the lane is hers, and your job is to deny her the isolated pick.

edits.before: Even in the late game Diana's all-in melee playstyle struggles to break through your poke and Mantra shields in a straight lane fight — she needs outside help (jungler, teammates) to actually punish you, since her damage alone rarely closes the gap fast enough. Keep poking from range, save your shield for her E-commitment, and don't get isolated in side lanes where she can jump you without backup. This phase remains yours to control unless she's clearly ahead on items or has fed elsewhere.
edits.after: Late, Diana's only problem was closing the gap and Moonfall solves it — she drags you and whoever stands near you into her burst from 475, and a single Soul Shield does not cover that. Play as pure peel: shield the target she lands on, W-root her off him, and never be the nearest body when her ult goes off. Hold Mantra for her commitment rather than for poke, and avoid side lanes where she can jump you with nobody to root her off. This phase is hers unless she is behind on items.

edits.before: You dominate this matchup from level 1 through the mid-game — Diana has to land her Q sphere before she can safely commit with E, and any whiffed attempt leaves her standing in your poke range with no escape. Punish every failed engage with Q/E trades and shield through the little damage she does land. Keep shoving to deny her easy CS and force her to either overextend into your poke or fall behind on gold. This is squarely your lane to control from minute one.
edits.after: You dominate this matchup from level 1 through level 5 — Diana needs Crescent Strike to mark you before Lunar Rush is free, and any whiffed arc leaves her standing in your 950 poke range with a 22s dash. Punish every failed engage with Q trades and shield through the little damage she does land. Keep shoving to deny her easy CS and force her to either overextend into your poke or fall behind on gold. This is squarely your lane to control until she hits 6.
